contexts.text: In this state all man's words, actions etc. are open.

How what is inward and what is outward act as one... take as an example an action, which unless it has charity or love and faith in it, and the Lord in them, is not an action that can be called a work of charity.
Anciently, action and will made one, from the action they plainly saw the will.
Treated of. AC 3293.

No one is ever rewarded there for good acts if he has placed merit in them... and no one is ever punished for evil acts, if he has acted from an end truly good; it is the ends that are regarded, the acts thence.
They are predicated according to the subject that is treated of.
Infants there are thus taught that they are not to think, speak and act from another.
Infants there who are of a celestial genius, think, speak and act more softly.
Such are therefore judged according to the acts of their life.
Although acts are not good in themselves, still they derive something of good from the end...
To the endeavour, but not to the act.
Thus he acts or seems to himself to act from what is good... and when truth and good act as one...
Of the giver and the receiver, as of the agent and the patient, a like state is perceived.
It then as it were spontaneously flows forth into act.
Disagreement in doctrinal things does not prevent the Church from being one if only there is unanimity as to willing well and acting well. Example(s).
When it is believed to be a matter of civil prudence to speak one thing and act another.
Divine order is terminated with man, in his actions, etc... the actions that flow from the will are not such things in the body as they are in the will.
The heart and lungs are the two founts of every action etc. of the body. AC 3887:2. Explained.
To know and to do good and truth is of the natural... when he perceives a delight in doing them...

So far as they receive from this new will, so far they receive also from these knowledges, and carry them into act, and believe; but so far as they do not receive from this new will, so far they are indeed able to learn such things, but not to carry them into act.
Man's thought, speech and action, which are the ultimate things of order, are nothing but truths from good.
The will flows into actions through muscular forms.
The will moves the muscles of the whole body, and thousands of scattered fibres to [produce] one action.
Endeavour produces acts and motions, and endeavour must be in an act or motion for it to exist and subsist.

What is implanted in man from childhood does not become his own until he acts according to it, and this from affection... it is no longer carried into act from knowledge or doctrine... he then no longer acts from memory, but from his own bent, so that at last they as it were spontaneously flow into act.
Embryos and newly born infants cannot have any... voluntary action until the lungs have been opened.
The influx of the one into the other (good and truth) causes them (spirits) spiritually to feel, and spiritually to act... hence is all perception and sensation, and all force and action.
To bear (children) = to acknowledge in faith and in act. Explained... The truths of faith not learned for the sake of acting... are inwardly against faith.

To acknowledge in faith and in act is to have a perception that it is so, and an affection that he wills it to be so, and this in every act of good... also a perception that good from proprium will necessarily have respect to self etc. in the good that it does.
Man then begins to be delighted with truth, first that he knows it, then that he acts according to it. Example(s).
A regenerate man does what is good from the affection of it... but one who is to be regenerated does what is good from the affection of truth...

The case is the same with every act of the body relatively to the inward things that are of thought and will; man's internal lives in his external by act or by acting; if the act or acting is not according to his internal, it is a sign either that it is not the internal that is producing the act, but a movement recurring from custom and habit; or...
Love is the willing of man, thence it is his thinking, and so it is his acting.
The influent action of these Spirits.
These Spirits suffer themselves to be acted upon.

Life with man flows in and acts into the various organs... the lungs act in one way and the heart in another, and so on; but still it is one life that actuates all so variously because it is differently received, for it is the form of anything according to which the action is determined.

There exists also a correspondence of the thoughts and affections with the actions and gestures of the body... hence such outward acts, because they correspond, are signs of inward things, and in them, as in all signs, there is an internal from which they take their quality...
Good is in the first place and is what principally acts...

Such is the perpetual circle with man; everything of knowledge and of thought is insinuated through either sight or hearing into thought, thence into the will, and from the will through thought into act... There is a similar circle from the memory, namely, from that sight through thought into the will, and from the will through thought into act; or if anything stands in the way while in the endeavour of acting, as soon as that is removed, it goes forth into act.

Thus do the truths of faith proceed from the will through thought into act, and if they cannot proceed into act, they are in endeavour; endeavour itself is inward act, for whenever the opportunity is given it becomes outward act.
Man then no longer acts from truth, but from good, that is, from charity, and he acts from charity when he lives according to the truths of faith, and loves doctrine for the sake of life.
The Israelites were required only to act what was representative of the Church.
Man's speech represents his thought, and his action represents his will.
Truth in the will and thence in act is called the good of truth... AC 4339. AC 4353:end. AC 5295. AC 5820. AC 5826:2.
Act precedes, the willing of man follows, for what a man acts from the understanding he at last acts from the will... he then no longer does what is good from truth, but from good.
Good is what acts and truth suffers itself to be acted upon. AC 5194.
Man then acts from good.
Truths of doctrine become goods when a man acts according to them; action itself so qualifies truths, for all action descends from the will.
When Evil Spirits and Angels combat, [the combat] is carried on about man and his eternal welfare, and it is carried on from the man...
It is all over with him. AC 5135:4.

Whether a man is natural or rational cannot be known to others from his speech, nor from his action, for the life of the thought that is in his speech and the life of the will that is in his action do not appear to any bodily sense... but in the other life that which is in speech and that which is in action are distinctly perceived by those who are in good.

If a man is rational he speaks from good thought and acts from good will, that is, he speaks from faith and acts from charity; but if a man is not rational he can then indeed by simulation act as rational, but...
He who is in any love continually thinks of the things that belong to it although he is in other things as to thought, speech and action.

In order that end, cause and effect may... act as one... since they correspond, the end can be in the cause, and actuate the cause, and the cause can be in the effect and actuate the effect, consequently the end through the cause can actuate the effect.

They then act as one; as for example, when heavenly love is the end, will the cause, and action the effect; if there is correspondence, then that love flows into will, and will into action, and thus they act as one, so that the action by correspondence may be as it were the love...

In everything of nature inwardly there is something acting from the spiritual world; unless this were so, nothing in the natural world would actuate the cause and the effect; that which is from the spiritual world in natural things is endeavour, on the ceasing of which action or motion ceases.

The case is the same as with the movements of the muscles, whence comes action... that this force or endeavour in action or motion is something spiritual in what is natural is clear, for to think and will is spiritual, whereas to act and to be moved is natural... That however which is in the will and thence in the thought is not similar in form to the action that it produces, for the action only represents that which the mind wills and thinks.
Thoughts are represented by the fibres, and the actions therefrom by the nerves, which [are formed] from the fibres.
All things of inward endeavour that are of the will... have outward acts or gestures corresponding to them, these acts or gestures flow from the correspondence itself.
In like manner it may be said of thought that it goes forth or proceeds when it becomes speech, and of the will when it becomes action. Explained.
The notion that freedom consists in thinking and willing from self, and in being able to act as one thinks and wills without check. AC 5462.
He who has learned truths not in order to will and do them...
Those things that are determined from thoughts into speech, and from will into acts in the body, flow ordinately into act by general influx, according to correspondences with the Grand Man.
The man who acts from truth is in truths through which is good, but he who acts from good is in truths that are from good.
It appears as if truths act of themselves, when they act reciprocally or react, but still truths do not act of themselves, but from the good that flows in.
So with him who in heart fears and honours God; that fear and honour are present in every single thing that he thinks, speaks and acts.
No one either in Heaven or Hell thinks, speaks, wills and acts from himself, but from others. Explained.

Spirits thus as it were act the man when with a man... but they are not permitted to enter so far as to the outward things that belong to actions and speech, for these come into act through general influx from the Lord without the mediation of particular Spirits and Angels: but although Spirits act as man... they do not know they are with a man. AC 5990.

I wondered why speech and action are not ruled by particular Spirits, like thought and will, but I have been instructed that speech follows from thought, and action from will, and that this flows from order, thus by general influx; but still there are Spirits assigned to every member of speech and to every member of action, but those Spirits do not know it. HH 296.
Since every agent has its own re-agent or reciprocal... and the agent is the cause and the re-agent the thing caused, therefore the reacting is also of the agent.
Good... actuates them to live according to truth... since they do not act from good but from truth...
As soon as a man who is in truth and not yet in good carries anything into act from a religious principle he afterwards defends it... for by act he imbues it and loves it. Example(s).
The reason why truth is strong is that good acts through truth. AC 6423:2.
Lest therefore a man, when in such a state, should act as he desires and speak as he thinks, he is kept in bonds...
The internal of the Church consists in willing what is good... and its external in doing it...
The movements of myriads of motor fibres concur to [produce] one action... and yet that little action appears simple and single. DP 199:3.
Since what is inward acts into what is outward, and not contrariwise, it is good that acts into truth.
Then because he wills the truth that he acknowledges, and acts according to it, it is appropriated to him.
That which acts inwardly prevails immensely over that which acts outwardly. Explained.
When truth becomes of life it is called good, but it is truth in act.
There is an image of marriage where there is an agent and a passive, and these must both be present for anything whatever to exist.
The sons of Simeon = the things of faith in act.
Unless this single substance reigned in the formations... that which is formed could not possibly subsist and act.
The state has not as yet been purified when man acts from the truth of faith, but it has when [he acts] from the good of charity, for then he acts from the will.
So did they = act from the will, for did they is repeated, and the first time it is mentioned it = act from the understanding.
The end is what determines actions, and gives quality to them.
(In temptations) Spirits from Hell excite and bring forth to view all the evil acts and thoughts of the man...
He who wants to be saved must... perform repentance. NJHD 159.
To perform repentance is... to carry on a new life... NJHD 161.
He who leads a life of faith daily performs repentance. NJHD 163.
After a man has performed repentance... NJHD 169.
Influx from the Divine passes first into perception, thence into will, and then into act, that is, into good work which is use, and there it stops.
Not to do any work on the Sabbath day = not to do anything from what is their own, but from the Lord, for the state of the Angels is that they will and do nothing from themselves.

Before regeneration, man acts from truth, and through it good is acquired... but after regeneration he acts from good, and by it truths are procured. Explained. AC 8510, Explained. AC 8516. AC 8516:3. AC 8539:end. Explained.
That they did not act according to Divine order. Signified, Explained.
Divine order is that the Lord should flow... through man's will into his action... AC 8516:3. Explained.
Books here = the recollection of all that they had done, for everyone carries with him into the other life the memory of all his acts...
No one however can judge any man according to his acts but the Lord, for all acts proceed from final causes that lie deeply hidden...
Hence it is evident that the book written = the presence of the acts of each and everyone.
When he begins no longer to act from truth but from good... when he acts from truth he is tempted... he then wills truths and does them...
In the first state when there is action from truth and not from good, good is as it were absent, but in the second state, when there is action from good, good is present...

When a man acts from truth and not as yet from good, he is in a state of undergoing temptations; through these he is progressively carried towards the second state, namely that he should act from good...
They do not will and act from anything but that the Word has so said. Signified.
Man is not regenerated until he acts from an affection of good...
The work that they shall do = faith in act, for it = action, here action from the light of intelligence... acknowledgement in act.
Hence the appearance that they act from themselves, but the perception that [they act] from the Lord...
The outward man then makes all good to consist in speaking well about the neighbour and in acting well towards him...
The man who is being regenerated is led by truth in order that he may be able to come to good, that is, to know it, afterwards to will it and at last to do it...
For then he no longer looks from truths [to see] what is to be believed and what is to be done...

They who suffer themselves to be regenerated, act from affection according to the precepts of faith, but they who only suffer themselves to be reformed, do not act from affection but from obedience. The difference explained... The latter do not do truth for the sake of truth, nor good for the sake of good. AC 8988. Treated of, Explained. AC 8991.
To act from purpose = from previous thought.
The more a man acts from the body, the less he acts from reason...

The inward Church is of the will and the outward of action, when the inward makes one with the outward, what is of the will is also of action, or what is the same, in action there is the will acting...
When truth... from the will goes forth into act, it becomes of man's life, and is called good.
Living motion which is action. No action can exist without will; the moment will ceases, so does action, wherefore the internal of action is will.
Will is the soul and the all in action, for when will ceases so does action.
Sensual men are cunning and dexterous in acting and reasoning.

There are action and reaction in all things that are conjoined, the agent is good and the reagent is truth; truth however never reacts from itself, but from good, thus so far as truth receives good, so far it reacts, and so far as it reacts, so far it is conjoined with it... perception is in itself reaction.
For act is endeavour acting, and thus the two are one... endeavour acting is called action...
So far as a man lives in Divine order... so far his acts are uses in form, and are correspondences, by which he is conjoined with Heaven.
Love in act is what remains, thus it is the life of man... love in act is work and deed.
Heaven and Hell... two opposites that act against each other, from whose action and reaction there results equilibrium... HH 537.

Without equilibrium there is not action and reaction, for equilibrium is between two forces of which one acts and the other reacts; rest from a like action and reaction is called equilibrium. Explained.
In the natural world that which acts and reacts is called force, and also endeavour, but in the spiritual world that which acts and reacts is called life and will...

There exists a spiritual equilibrium between good acting on the one hand and evil reacting on the other, or between evil acting and good reacting; the former equilibrium exists with the good, the latter with the evil.
The doctrinal things of the Church do not enter a man's life until they enter into his will and thence into his actions...
The Word treats of the Lord alone.

In everything created by God there is reaction; in life alone is there action, and reaction is excited through the action of life, this reaction appears as if it were of the created thing, from the fact that it exists when it is actuated.

Hence man from his hereditary evil reacts against God; but if he believes that all good of life is from the action of God, and all evil of life from the reaction of man, reaction thus becomes of action, and man acts with God as if from himself. The equilibrium of all things is from simultaneous action and reaction.
For what is natural to act into what is spiritual is altogether against order.
It appears as if the agent or efficient exists by itself, but this is an appearance...

In a series of similar degrees are also affection, thought and action; because all affection has relation to love, thought to wisdom and action to use... all things of thought and affection are present in action.
The ultimate of each series, which is use, action, work and exercise, is the aggregate and containant of all the prior things. Explained.
Thus everything of the will and thought are in the action...
Living motion in man is action, which is produced by these forces from the will united to the understanding... the forces are not in power except through the action of the body.
The appearance that sometimes there is endeavour and force without action. Explained.
From the action alone, done by the hands, the Angels with a man know his whole quality... DLW 279, Explained.

In the greatest and least things of the universe, both living and dead, there are action and reaction; hence is the equilibrium of all things, which is taken away when action exceeds reaction, and contrariwise. (This principle applied to the action and reaction of the natural mind and the action and reaction of the spiritual mind, and fully explained.)

That all things of the three degrees of the natural mind are included in works done by acts of the body. General article. The acts or works themselves appear [simple] but there are innumerable things in them. Explained. DLW 278, Explained.
Before the Angels, every act of a spiritual man is like delicious, useful and beautiful fruit.
Acts and works are ultimates. DLW 316:4.
The Spiritual impels nature to act, as a living thing impels a dead one.

An act of the body from love without understanding is like an act of a man in the night, for the man does not then know what he is doing; thus in the act there would be nothing of intelligence and wisdom; such an act cannot be called a living act, for an act derives its being from love and its quality from intelligence.
How it is that those who are in infernal love can speak and act like those who are in spiritual love.
It is a law of the Divine Providence that man should act from freedom according to reason. General article.
The effects of the spirit, even if they do not come into the act of the body, are still as if in act when there is consent.
When a mere miracle moves a man to piety, etc., he acts merely from the natural man...
Whatever a man... acts from will is appropriated to him... Explained.
The Lord's presence... is in the smallest particulars of man's speech and action. Explained.
All man's action also flows in. Explained.
Under Self, see this reference.
(The solifidian idea of the act of justification or of faith in act. Explained and refuted.) TCR 505.
Will and understanding are nothing without action. Explained. TCR 387:4.

Will or endeavour is act in itself, because it is a constant effort to act, which also becomes outward act when a determination is come to; wherefore endeavour and will, as an inward act, are accepted by every wise man, because they are accepted by God, altogether as an outward act, if only it does not fail when opportunity is given. TCR 387:6.

What is a man's action unless it is the mind acting?... Wherefore when the mind is led by the Lord, the action also is led, and the mind and action therefrom are led by the Lord when we believe in Him... If the mind is charity, the action also is charity, but if the mind is faith alone, the action also is that faith... TCR 461:14.
Wherefore the speech and action that flow forth from thought, do not flow forth from thought, but from love through thought.
From the will, which in itself is spiritual, flow forth actions...

In all conjunction by love there must be action, reception and reaction; the delicious state of a wife's love is acting or action, the state of a husband's wisdom is recipient or reception and is also reacting or reaction according to perception, and this reaction is perceived by wives with delights in the bosom...
The enormity that God pays no attention to a man's acts, but to faith only... BE 67.
Influx into speech takes place from the will through the understanding, but influx into actions from the understanding through the will.

In a state of conjunction with God, man acts as in the former state, but now from God, and it is not necessary that he should now, as before, attribute to God all the good that he wills and does... because this is inscribed on his heart, and thence is inwardly in every action.

This may be illustrated by the action of the heart in the lungs and into them, and by the reaction of the lungs of themselves from the heart... it is the same with the action of the heart in and into all the viscera.

Hereditary evil acts in man and into man, in like manner good from the Lord... if they were to act through man, he would not be reformable, but since both depend on man's free choice, he becomes guilty when he acts of himself from evil, and guiltless when [he acts] of himself from good...
So also does the internal of man act in the external and into it, but it does not act through the external...

When the Word is in some degree of fulness in the internal of a man, he speaks and acts of himself from the Word, and not the Word through him... The Lord also from Himself or from the Word acts in man and into him, but not through him, because man acts and speaks freely from the Lord when [he acts and speaks] from the Word.
The soul acts in the body and into it, but not through it, and the body acts of itself from the soul. Explained.
When the inward man wills well and the outward acts well, both make one... but if the inward man wills evilly, and still the outward acts well, he nevertheless acts from Hell...
They can act as one actually, and they can act as one apparently...
Action and reaction produce this conjunction of the heart with the blood... There is a like action and reaction between the embryo and the uterus.
But the conjunction of the Lord and man is not effected by act and react, but by cooperations, for the Lord acts and man receives action from Him, and operates as of himself...
Such is the conjunction of will and action.
In operating, these three loves are like will, understanding and action; the will flows into the understanding and there looks out for itself means, by which it produces action.
All man's action and speech proceed from the lower region of the mind directly, and from its higher region indirectly. TCR 420:2.
It is acts of repentance that form the Church with a man; acts of repentance are...
That true repentance is to examine not only the acts of one's life, but also the intentions of one's will. General article.
Action is the will acting...

In all motion, and thence in all action, there are an active and a passive, that is, the agent acts, and the patient acts from the agent, hence there is one action from both. Example(s)... As to charity and faith, the Lord acts and man acts from Him, for the active of the Lord is in the passive of man, wherefore the power of acting well is from the Lord, and thence the will of acting is as of the man, because he is in free determination, from which he is able to act together with the Lord, and so to conjoin himself, and he is [also] able to act from the power of Hell, which is outside, and so to separate himself. The concordant action of man with the action of the Lord is what is here understood by cooperation.

Action and cooperation such as have been described, may be seen in everything that is in any activity and mobility; such is the action and cooperation of the heart and all its arteries; the heart acts, and the arteries cooperate... Other examples given.
The Lord alone acts, and man suffers himself to be acted upon, and cooperates to all appearance as from himself, although inwardly from God.
Hence it is that from a single action of man the Angels perceive the quality of his will...
As will is in action...
Wherefore all things that proceed from man, whether action or conversation, make the man, and are the man himself.
On the multitude of Spirits who concur to one single action of man.
In order to appropriation and conjunction there must be action and reaction. Explained. AE 616:2.
Nothing can act or move unless it is between two forces, of which one acts and the other reacts.
Hence it is that the will and the act are one.
3. Hence love acts and wisdom reacts, and by this reciprocality every effect exists.
